newsitem.title: USA: Republicans canvass 10,000 brand-new U.S. citizens.
newsitem.headline: Republicans canvass 10,000 brand-new U.S. citizens.

text.p: More than 10,000 immigrants were sworn in as U.S. citizens on Tuesday at Texas' largest-ever naturalisation ceremony and immediately received an appeal to vote Republican.

As about 10,300 newly naturalised citizens waved U.S. flags and sang "America the Beautiful" during the ceremony in Texas Stadium in Dallas, a light plane flew overhead, trailing a banner that read: "Felicidades. Vota Dole-Kemp" (Spanish for "Congratulations. Vote Dole-Kemp").

Texas is a must-win state for Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole and his running mate, Jack Kemp. Hispanic immigrants, widely seen as being predominantly Democratic, were easily the biggest ethnic group at Tuesday's event.
Held to mark Citizenship Day, the emotional ceremony took place inside the home stadium of the Super Bowl champion Dallas Cowboys, dubbed "America's Team" by their supporters.
People from 113 countries, seated in the bleachers on one side of the stadium, recited their oaths in unison and cheered when told they were now U.S. citizens.
Many said they would vote in the Nov. 5 presidential and congressional elections.

"Of course. It is my God-given right," said Henry Emblin, an accountant who was born in Nigeria but has spent the last 17 years in the United States. "I feel very American. I feel I contribute to this country."
Doris Meissner, a commissioner of the Immigration and Naturalisation Service, told the new U.S. citizens they had chosen to join the "most enduring democracy ever created."
About half the new citizens were Mexican, the predominant immigrant group in the Southwest.
Another 10,000 immigrants were to be sworn in at a similar ceremony in San Jose, Calif., Wednesday.
